title: Wasserstein Stability, Couplings Across Volumes, and the $1+1/d$ Moment Thresholds in the Edwards--Anderson Model
authors: Mauris Chueng, Hexiang Wang, Keheng Zhu
abstract: We study the quenched pressure of the nearest-neighbor Edwards--Anderson Ising model with free and periodic boundary conditions. First, we prove that the infinite-volume pressure is $βd$-Lipschitz in the coupling law for the $1$-Wasserstein distance, yielding quantitative thermodynamic limits for spatially inhomogeneous disorder. Second, for periodic volumes, we prove that almost-sure convergence under every joint coupling of the finite-volume disorder arrays is equivalent to complete convergence of the one-volume pressure laws. Third, we prove that $\mathbb{E}\vert{}J\vert{}^{1+1/d}<\infty$ guarantees this universal-coupling conclusion. We further show that this exponent is optimal among uniform power-moment assumptions: for every $1\leq q<1+1/d$, there is a centered symmetric law with finite $q$-th moment for which canonical nested volumes converge almost surely, whereas independently resampled volumes with the same fixed-volume marginals converge in probability but not almost surely. Finally, in dimension one, we prove that the first-moment condition is also necessary for a finite limiting pressure.
summary: This paper rigorously analyzes the thermodynamic limit of the Edwards-Anderson Ising model under random disorder. It proves that the convergence of the system's pressure to a stable infinite-volume limit depends critically on the disorder couplings having a finite moment of order $1+1/d$. This threshold exponent is shown to be sharp, providing deep mathematical insight into the role of disorder fluctuations.
main_problem: The paper investigates the stability and convergence of the quenched pressure in the Edwards-Anderson Ising model when the disorder couplings are spatially inhomogeneous.
main_result: It establishes that the existence of a universal-coupling limit for the pressure requires the disorder couplings to satisfy the moment condition $\mathbb{E}|J|^{1+1/d} < \infty$, and this exponent is proven to be optimal.
method: The analysis combines concepts from probability theory, specifically using the 1-Wasserstein distance to quantify stability, and employing strong limit theorems (like Borel-Cantelli) to relate convergence in probability to almost sure convergence.
model_or_system: The system is the nearest-neighbor Edwards-Anderson Ising model, characterized by random couplings $J_{x,i}$ on a lattice $\Lambda_L$. The study focuses on the quenched pressure, defined as the normalized logarithm of the partition function, $p^L( eta, J)$.
key_observables: The quenched pressure, $p_b^L( eta, J)$, and its convergence properties under different boundary conditions (free vs. periodic).
important_parameters: The spatial dimension $d$, the inverse temperature $ eta$, and the critical moment exponent $1+1/d$.
main_assumptions: The disorder $\{J_{x,i}\}$ is assumed to be i.i.d. initially, but the core results extend to spatially inhomogeneous disorder, requiring analysis via joint couplings across volumes.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes basic convergence results using the 1-Wasserstein distance for the free/periodic pressures. It then develops the universal-coupling criterion, culminating in the proof that the $1+1/d$ moment condition is necessary and sufficient for this strong convergence property.
why_interesting: While focused on classical statistical mechanics, the rigorous mathematical tools developed—especially the analysis of convergence thresholds based on moment conditions and coupling stability—are highly relevant to understanding critical phenomena in complex, disordered quantum systems.
